backlink_pages.title: Runbook — Worker Lease Exhaustion
backlink_pages.author: Sam Ortiz
backlink_pages.excerpt: Symptoms Long-running exports hold a lease until the heartbeat expires (NMA-114). Concurrency semaphores leak slots after a panicked handler (NMA-124). Nested null optional fields in job payloads

backlink_pages.title: Observability Standards
backlink_pages.author: Jordan Lee
backlink_pages.excerpt: Tracing Webhook fan-out traces under NMA-170 use the shared trace context. Worker crashes when payloads contain nested null optional fields—see NMA-108—must include job type attributes on the span.

content.text: No crashes in 12h soak on staging with the null fuzzer. Deployed.
Export and reindex workers crash hard when a job payload includes nested optional fields explicitly set to null. The panic is a null pointer during struct decode, not a handled validation error.

Payloads with nested null optionals should either coerce to omitted or reject with a permanent failure reason. Instead the worker process exits, the job returns to the queue, and the crash loop burns the pod restart budget.

Hypothesis: the generated payload structs use nested value types rather than pointers/Option, so unmarshalling cannot represent null and aborts. Top-level nulls are fine; only nested optionals trip it.
Long-running export queues stall whenever a client omits a filter by sending null instead of leaving the key out.
